A.best_shot: shots seed 3, up the road to the ice (dark cave mouth under the ledge)
A.why: Glacier pour is a box clutter with no silhouette; tongue always on the north edge; meltwater effect barely visible.

B.best_shot: shots seed 3, the crossing from the south
B.why: Bridge over a stepped crevasse is a clear subject and the crossing angle varies well; crevasse floor is checkerboard paving with no glow.

C.best_shot: shots seed 2, the lip and the spire
C.why: Best set piece of the run and a real vertical shaft; every seed is the same round well with a heavy teal rim.

D.best_shot: shots seed 2, the arch on the crest
D.why: Good seed variety, but fins read as bleachers, grey on grey, and the spindrift is muddy.

E.best_shot: shots seed 3, the road in (vent with ice teeth in the foreground)
E.why: Vents, ice crowns, terraces and a strong frost-steam column; clusters vary per seed; ground over-cluttered with spikes.

F.best_shot: shots seed 1, the wreck from the ice
F.why: The ship is the strongest single subject; hull glow reads as a pipe and the game camera turns the mast into scribbles.

G.why: Barrows don't read as mounds, shots are nearly black, one oval layout jittered across seeds.

H.why: Column rows to an altar compose well, but all twelve seeds are the same plan and the frost shafts are faint.

notes: E, F, B and C are close (6.8-7.1) and all worth carrying forward: E for completeness, F for the strongest subject, B for the clearest readable crossing, C for the best effect. C's aurora column could also be borrowed for E's vents. G and A lack a readable subject; H needs layout variety before anything else.
